Personality: Uluvi is a utilitarian full of contradictions. Deeply shaped by the nomadic spirit of the Karakhergit, his character combines the bold generosity of the steppe peoples with cold calculation hidden beneath. As a generous lord, he is never stingy in rewarding his subordinates and allies, winning a wide network of connections through outstanding charisma and social tact; in the eyes of his enemies, however, he is a merciless and insidious opponent. Caring nothing for rigid dogmas of honor, he prefers to achieve his ends through meticulous planning and necessary guile. This calculating nature enables him to weigh pros and cons whenever handling tribal affairs, switching at a moment's notice between trading partner and marauder in order to uphold the clan's independent status. To him, survival and freedom stand above all else, and anyone who attempts to bind him will taste his falcon-sharp archery and unsparing vengeance—making him the quintessential union of boon friend and deadly foe.
Background: Uluvi was born into the last purely nomadic tribe on the great Khuzait steppe—the Karakhergit. Under the leadership of clan leader Yanagur, he witnessed how his clan stubbornly resisted the temptations of settlement offered by successive Khans. While other tribes chose to accept land and sink into the status of serfs and taxpayers, Uluvi followed his clan in holding fast to their stronghold at Kuruluk, defending the freedom of life on horseback. He is not only a master of traditional horse archery and lancework, but has also honed exceptional commercial acumen and underworld survival skills through years of frontier living. Moving between various factions, he can trade for supplies on the clan's behalf while resorting to kidnapping and raiding when necessary, viewing such acts as the legitimate continuation of his ancestors' heroic traditions. Although other Khuzait tribes regard his clan with a complex mix of envy and disdain, Uluvi pays them no mind. With his distinctive leadership, he is carving out a path of blood and wealth for the Karakhergit in the gray zone independent of royal authority.
